tools.name: consumption-history_get-per-branch-v2
tools.description: Returns consumption metrics for each branch across one or more projects listed in `project_ids` (1 to 100 projects). params.name: limit

params.name: project_ids

params.name: branch_ids

The specified `date-time` value must respect the specified `granularity`: - For `hourly`, consumption metrics are limited to the last 168 hours. - For `daily`, consumption metrics are limited to the last 60 days. - For `monthly`, consumption metrics are limited to the last year. Branch-level metrics are returned from when the account first ingests branch-level consumption data. Periods before that time contain no branch metrics.

Values are write-only: they are encrypted at rest, and responses carry only the variable names (the `environment` array), never the values.

params.name: zip
params.description: Optional ZIP archive of the function source code. Omit to reuse the latest version's bundle (a config-only change). Required for the first deployment of a function. Place `index.mjs` or `index.js` at the archive root, without a containing directory. If both exist, `index.mjs` is loaded. Export a request handler function or an object with a `fetch` method. Use `export default` for ESM or `module.exports` for CommonJS; prefer `index.mjs` for ESM. Upload JavaScript ready to run on Node.js 24. Compile TypeScript before uploading. Bundle dependencies into the entry module, or include the required modules and assets in the archive with their relative paths preserved (including `node_modules` for external packages). Node.js built-in modules do not need to be bundled. The API does not transpile, bundle, or install dependencies. The ZIP is limited to 32 MiB compressed and 128 MiB extracted, with at most 32,768 entries and 64 MiB per file. Bundle large dependency trees to keep the archive small. ZIPs larger than 32 MiB are rejected with HTTP 413 before creating a deployment. The extracted-size, entry-count, and per-file limits are enforced during the asynchronous build; an accepted upload that exceeds them fails the build. For example, a self-contained ESM bundle needs only `index.mjs` at the ZIP root. The Neon CLI bundles source into this layout by default; `neon function deploy --no-bundle` packages a prebuilt directory or an entry file named `index.mjs` or `index.js`.

Returns array of string.

tools.name: projects_branches_presign-project-branch-bucket-object
tools.description: Returns a presigned URL that transfers bytes directly to or from the object's bucket on the specified branch, without the caller ever handling S3 credentials. The `operation` field selects the direction: - `upload` returns a presigned `PUT` URL (the caller `PUT`s the file bytes straight to `url` with the returned `headers`). Authorized with project write access. - `download` returns a presigned `GET` URL (the caller `GET`s the bytes straight from `url`). Authorized with project read access. The platform mints a short-lived credential and builds the SigV4-signed URL against the branch's S3 data-plane host, returning it together with the HTTP method, any headers the caller must echo, and the URL's expiry. Served by the user's session (no customer S3 credentials required). **Note**: This endpoint is currently in Beta. Required: project_id, branch_id, bucket_name, object_key, operation. Optional: content_type, expires_in_seconds (default: 900).

params.name: object_key
params.description: The object key. Keys may contain `/`; the `/` characters of nested keys must be...

params.name: content_type
params.description: The `Content-Type` to bind into the signed request. Only meaningful for `upload`: when set, the caller MUST send the same `Content-Type` header on the `PUT`, and the value is echoed back in the response `headers`. Ignored for `download`.

params.name: expires_in_seconds
params.description: How long the presigned URL stays valid, in seconds. Defaults to 900 (15 minutes); capped at 604800 (7 days).

params.name: operation
params.description: The transfer direction. `upload` returns a presigned `PUT` URL; `download` returns a presigned `GET` URL.

tools.name: projects_branches_query-project-branch-logs
tools.description: Returns logs emitted by services running on the specified branch, ordered by timestamp according to `sort_order`. All supplied filters are combined with `AND`: a record is returned only when it matches every filter. `minimum_severity` and `severity_text` are independent filters, so setting both requires a record to clear the severity floor *and* match the exact severity text. Supply `logql` instead of the structured filters to run a raw LogQL expression. Combining it with any structured filter is rejected rather than silently ignored; `limit`, `sort_order`, and the time window still apply, because those bound the query rather than form part of the expression. Give the window either as `since` — a duration ending at `end_time`, or at the current time when `end_time` is omitted — or as an explicit `start_time`. Supplying both is rejected. A single response holds at most 1,000 records. When `is_truncated` is `true`, pass the returned `next_cursor` back as `cursor` to fetch the next page, repeating the time range and every filter unchanged. If no time range is supplied, the query covers the previous hour. The maximum supported time range is seven days. `end_time` is exclusive. **Note**: This endpoint is currently in Private Beta. Required: project_id, branch_id. Optional: body_contains, cursor, end_time (plus 11 more).

params.name: body_contains
params.description: Match records whose rendered `message` contains this case-sensitive substring. Records with a structured body are matched against their JSON rendering, so the substring meets JSON syntax rather than prose: a bare key name such as `operation` matches every record carrying that key, and `http_status: 200` matches none, because the rendering contains `'http_status':200` with no space.

params.name: cursor
params.description: Opaque pagination cursor returned as `next_cursor` by a previous call. Resume the query after the last record of the previous page, repeating the time range and every filter unchanged.

params.name: end_time
params.description: Exclusive end of the query window. Defaults to the current time.

params.name: limit
params.description: Maximum number of log records to return per page.

params.name: logql
params.description: Escape hatch for selections the structured filters cannot express: a raw LogQL expression, evaluated against this branch's log stream. Only stream selectors and line filters are accepted — no aggregations and no parser stages. Supplying this alongside any structured filter is rejected with `conflicting_filters` rather than silently ignoring one of them. `limit`, `sort_order`, and the time window still apply. This field passes the underlying query language through to the caller, so unlike the rest of this contract it may change as that backend changes. Prefer the structured filters where they suffice.

params.name: minimum_severity
params.description: An OpenTelemetry severity level. A minimum severity includes every higher level in this order: `trace`, `debug`, `info`, `warn`, `error`, `fatal`.

params.name: scope_name
params.description: Match the OpenTelemetry instrumentation scope name exactly.

params.name: service_name
params.description: Match the OpenTelemetry `service.name` resource attribute exactly.

params.name: severity_text
params.description: Match the OpenTelemetry severity text exactly.

params.name: since
params.description: Length of the query window, ending at `end_time` or at the current time when `end_time` is omitted. Mutually exclusive with `start_time`. Prefer this over computing absolute bounds when the caller only means 'the last hour'.

params.name: sort_order
params.description: Order matching records by timestamp. `desc`, the default, returns the newest records first.

params.name: source
params.description: The Neon service that emitted the log record.

params.name: start_time
params.description: Inclusive beginning of the query window. Mutually exclusive with `since`. Defaults to one hour before `end_time`, or one hour before the current time when both bounds are omitted.

params.name: trace_id
params.description: Match records associated with this OpenTelemetry trace ID. W3C Trace Context defines a trace ID as 32 lowercase hex digits, and that is what is stored, so an uppercase value is rejected rather than silently matching nothing.

tools.name: projects_branches_register-project-branch-custom-domain
tools.description: Registers a customer-owned domain (for example `dashboard.acme.com`) on the branch and points it at a target entity, chosen by `entity_type` + `entity_id`. In v1 only `entity_type: function` is supported (an unsupported type is rejected with `400`), where `entity_id` is the function slug and the function must already exist on the branch (else `404`). The response includes the `cname_target` the customer must point their domain at with a CNAME record; the domain goes live only once that DNS resolves and a certificate is issued on the first request. A domain already registered to another resource is rejected with `409` and no detail about the owner. Re-registering the same domain for the same entity is idempotent. **Note**: This endpoint is currently in Beta. Required: project_id, branch_id, domain, entity_id, entity_type. Returns the new CustomDomain.

params.name: domain
params.description: The custom domain to register (for example `dashboard.acme.com`). Case-insensitive; normalized to lowercase (a trailing root dot is stripped, so the 254-char bound admits a fully-qualified name whose normalized form is 253 chars). Neon-managed and internal hostnames are rejected.

params.name: entity_id
params.description: The target entity's identifier within the branch. For `function` this is the function slug (which must already exist on the branch).

params.name: entity_type
params.description: The kind of branch entity to point the domain at. v1 supports only `function`; any other value is rejected with `invalid_entity_type`.

tools.description: Resets the password for the specified Postgres role. Returns a new password and operations. The new password is ready to use when the last operation finishes. The old password remains valid until last operation finishes. Connections to the compute endpoint are dropped. If idle, the compute endpoint becomes active for a short period of time. For related information, see [Manage roles](https://neon.com/docs/manage/roles/). Required: project_id, branch_id, role_name.

tools.name: projects_branches_restore-project-branch
tools.description: Restores a branch to an earlier state in its own or another branch's history by specifying an LSN or timestamp. Creates a new branch from the historical state. Required: project_id, branch_id, source_branch_id. Optional: preserve_under_name, source_lsn, source_timestamp. Returns the new BranchOperations.

params.name: preserve_under_name
params.description: Name under which to save the current branch state before restoring. Required when the branch has children or when `source_branch_id` equals the branch being restored; in those cases all existing child branches are moved to the newly created branch. If omitted and not required, the previous state is not preserved.

params.name: source_branch_id
params.description: The `branch_id` of the restore source branch. If `source_timestamp` and `source_lsn` are omitted, the branch will be restored to head. If `source_branch_id` is equal to the branch's id, `source_timestamp` or `source_lsn` is required.

params.name: source_lsn
params.description: A Postgres LSN (for example, `0/1A2B3C4`) on the source branch to restore from. Mutually exclusive with `source_timestamp`. Omit both to restore to head.

params.name: source_timestamp
params.description: A point in time on the source branch to restore from, in RFC 3339 format. When omitted alongside `source_lsn`, the branch is restored to the latest available state of the source branch.

tools.name: projects_branches_reveal-credential
tools.description: Returns the live `api_token` and `s3_secret_access_key` of an existing credential, so a credential whose issuance response was lost can be recovered without minting a new one. This is a POST with an explicit `/reveal` verb so the secrets never ride a GET, where they would land in access logs, browser history and proxy caches. Revoked and expired credentials return 404, as does a `token_id` that does not belong to this project. A credential issued before secret retrieval was supported has no recoverable secret and returns 409 — rotate it to obtain one. **Note**: This endpoint is currently in Beta. Required: project_id, branch_id, token_id.

tools.name: projects_branches_revoke-credential
tools.description: Soft-deletes the credential. Idempotent. **Note**: This endpoint is currently in Beta. Required: project_id, branch_id, token_id. Destructive.

tools.name: projects_branches_rotate-credential
tools.description: Replaces the secret material on an existing scoped credential in place. `token_id` is preserved — it is the `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` for S3-compatible clients, so the access key id your application already holds keeps working and only the secret changes. This is the analog of resetting a Postgres password, not of issuing a second credential. The response carries the new `api_token` and `s3_secret_access_key` exactly once. Rotation is **not** idempotent: retrying after an ambiguous timeout mints another secret and supersedes the previous replacement, so a retry does not recover a lost response — it only invalidates the secret you did not receive. If you lose the response, issue a replacement credential and revoke this one. The old secret stops authenticating as soon as the rotation commits. Where a region caches credentials on its data-plane verifiers, a replica may briefly keep accepting the old secret — and rejecting the new one — until its cache entry expires; where it does not, the cutover is immediate apart from requests already in flight. Either way the changeover is not atomic across replicas, so retry an unexpected authentication failure right after rotating rather than treating the new secret as bad. `last_used_at` continues to report the logical credential's prior usage and says nothing about whether the new secret has been used yet. Only a live, unexpired, unrevoked customer-managed (`user`) credential on a live project and live branch is eligible. Anything else — including the platform-internal `function` and `system` credentials — is reported as not found, indistinguishable from an unknown `token_id`. **Note**: This endpoint is currently in Beta. Required: project_id, branch_id, token_id. Returns array of GrantedCredentialScope.

tools.name: projects_branches_rotate-project-branch-realtime-secret
tools.description: Replaces the branch's Realtime shared secret. Rotation is asynchronous: once the Realtime state is no longer pending, the previous secret stops working and `GET /projects/{project_id}/branches/{branch_id}/realtime/secret` returns the new one. Required: project_id, branch_id.

tools.name: projects_branches_send-neon-auth-email-provider-test
tools.description: Sends a test email using the branch's already-saved custom SMTP configuration. Only the `recipient_email` is provided — the stored SMTP settings and password are used server-side, so the caller does not need to re-supply (or be able to read) the password. This avoids the GET response's masked password being sent back, which would fail SMTP authentication. Requires a configured custom SMTP provider on a Better Auth integration. A shared provider, a missing configuration, or a non-Better-Auth integration is rejected. Required: project_id, branch_id, recipient_email. Returns the new SendNeonAuthTestEmailResponse.

params.name: recipient_email
params.description: The email address to send the test email to.

tools.name: projects_branches_send-neon-auth-test-email
tools.description: Sends a test email using the SMTP server settings supplied in the request body to verify connectivity and credentials. The request body must include the full SMTP server settings (`host`, `port`, `username`, `password`, `sender_email`, `sender_name`) and the `recipient_email` address. Deprecated: to test a branch's already-saved configuration, use `sendNeonAuthEmailProviderTest`, which reuses the stored SMTP password server-side so the caller never has to re-supply (or be able to read) it. This endpoint remains available for testing an unsaved full configuration and for non-Better-Auth providers. Required: project_id, branch_id, host, password, port, recipient_email, sender_email, sender_name, username. Returns the new SendNeonAuthTestEmailResponse.

params.name: password
params.description: Password for authenticating with the SMTP server.

params.name: port
params.description: TCP port of the SMTP server. Common values: 25 (SMTP), 465 (SMTPS), 587 (submission).

params.name: recipient_email
params.description: The email address to send the test email to.

params.name: sender_email
params.description: Email address used as the From address on outgoing auth emails.

params.name: sender_name
params.description: Display name shown as the sender in outgoing emails.

params.name: username
params.description: Username for authenticating with the SMTP server.

tools.name: projects_branches_set-default-project-branch
tools.description: Sets the specified branch as the project's default branch. The default designation is automatically removed from the previous default branch. For more information, see [Manage branches](https://neon.com/docs/manage/branches/). Required: project_id, branch_id. Returns the new BranchOperations.

tools.name: projects_branches_set-snapshot-schedule
tools.description: Updates the backup schedule for the specified branch. The schedule defines how often automatic snapshots are created (for example, `daily` or `weekly`). Requires a paid plan. Required: project_id, branch_id, schedule. Returns the updated EmptyResponse.

params.name: schedule
params.description: List of schedule entries defining the backup frequency. At least one entry is required.

tools.name: projects_branches_start-anonymization
tools.description: Starts the anonymization process for an anonymized branch that is in the initialized, error, or anonymized state. This will apply all defined masking rules to anonymize sensitive data in the branch databases. The branch must be an anonymized branch to start anonymization. **Note**: This endpoint is currently in Beta. Required: project_id, branch_id. Returns the new AnonymizedBranchStatusResponse.

tools.name: projects_branches_update-branch-neon-auth-oauth-provider
tools.description: Updates an OAuth provider for the specified project. Required: project_id, branch_id, oauth_provider_id (default: google). Optional: client_id, client_secret, microsoft_tenant_id. Returns the updated NeonAuthOauthProvider.

params.name: client_id
params.description: The OAuth client ID registered with the provider. Omit to keep the currently configured value.

params.name: client_secret
params.description: OAuth client secret for the provider. Omit to leave the existing secret unchanged.

params.name: microsoft_tenant_id
params.description: The tenant ID scoping the Microsoft OAuth provider. Supply this field when the provider type is microsoft; it has no effect for other provider types.

tools.name: projects_branches_update-masking-rules
tools.description: Updates the masking rules for the specified anonymized branch. Masking rules define how sensitive data should be anonymized using PostgreSQL Anonymizer. **Note**: This endpoint is currently in Beta. Required: project_id, branch_id, masking_rules. Returns array of MaskingRule.

params.name: masking_rules
params.description: List of masking rules to apply to the branch. This will replace all existing masking rules for the branch.

tools.name: projects_branches_update-neon-auth-allow-localhost
tools.description: Updates the localhost allow setting for the specified branch's Neon Auth integration. When enabled, authentication flows work from `localhost` without adding it to the redirect URI whitelist. Required: project_id, branch_id, allow_localhost. Returns the updated NeonAuthAllowLocalhostResponse.

tools.name: projects_branches_update-neon-auth-config
tools.description: Updates the auth configuration for the branch. Currently supports updating the application name used in auth emails. Required: project_id, branch_id, name. Returns the updated NeonAuthConfigResponse.

params.name: name
params.description: The application name used in auth emails and communications.

tools.name: projects_branches_update-neon-auth-email-and-password-config
tools.description: Updates the email and password authentication configuration for the specified branch's Neon Auth integration. Only the fields provided in the request body are updated. Required: project_id, branch_id. Optional: auto_sign_in_after_verification, disable_sign_up, email_verification_method (plus 4 more). Returns the updated NeonAuthEmailAndPasswordConfig.

params.name: auto_sign_in_after_verification
params.description: Whether users are automatically signed in after verifying their email

params.name: disable_sign_up
params.description: Whether to disable new user sign ups. When omitted, the current setting is not changed.

params.name: email_verification_method
params.description: The email verification method to use. - `link`: Sends a verification link via email - `otp`: Sends a one-time password (OTP) via email

params.name: enabled
params.description: Controls whether email and password authentication is enabled for this project. When omitted from an update request, the current value is unchanged.

params.name: require_email_verification
params.description: When true, users must verify their email address before they can sign in. Omitting this field from an update request leaves the current value unchanged.

params.name: send_verification_email_on_sign_in
params.description: Whether to send a verification email when a user with an unverified email signs in.

params.name: send_verification_email_on_sign_up
params.description: Whether to send a verification email when users sign up.

tools.name: projects_branches_update-neon-auth-email-provider
tools.description: Updates the email provider configuration for the specified branch's Neon Auth integration. The email provider handles transactional messages such as verification emails and password reset links. Partial `standard` updates — omitting fields to keep their stored values — are supported only for Better Auth integrations, which merge omitted fields server-side. Legacy Stack Auth integrations do not merge and require all six `standard` fields (`host`, `port`, `username`, `password`, `sender_email`, `sender_name`) on every update; a partial `standard` body is rejected with 400. Required: project_id, branch_id. Returns the updated NeonAuthEmailServerConfigResponse.

tools.name: projects_branches_update-neon-auth-magic-link-plugin
tools.description: Updates the magic link plugin configuration for Neon Auth. The magic link plugin enables passwordless authentication via email magic links. Required: project_id, branch_id. Optional: disable_sign_up, enabled, expires_in. Returns the updated NeonAuthMagicLinkConfig.

params.name: disable_sign_up
params.description: When true, sign-up via magic link is disabled.

params.name: enabled
params.description: Whether to enable the magic link plugin.

params.name: expires_in
params.description: Minutes until the magic link expires.

tools.name: projects_branches_update-neon-auth-organization-plugin
tools.description: Updates the organization plugin configuration for Neon Auth. The organization plugin enables multi-tenant organization support. Required: project_id, branch_id. Optional: creator_role, enabled, membership_limit (plus 2 more). Returns the updated NeonAuthOrganizationConfig.

params.name: creator_role
params.description: Role of the organization's creator. `owner`: full control, including deleting the org and transferring ownership. `admin`: manage members and settings only.

params.name: enabled
params.description: Controls whether the organization plugin is active for the organization.

params.name: organization_limit
params.description: Maximum organizations a user can belong to (created or joined). At the limit, the user cannot create or join more.

params.name: send_invitation_email
params.description: When true, invited users receive an email containing an accept link. Requires that the invited user has a verified email address.

tools.name: projects_branches_update-neon-auth-phone-number-plugin
tools.description: Updates the phone number plugin configuration for Neon Auth. Only the fields provided in the request body are updated; omitted fields retain their current values. The phone number plugin enables phone-based OTP authentication. OTP codes are delivered via the `send.otp` webhook event with `delivery_preference: 'sms'`. A webhook must be configured with the `send.otp` event enabled for SMS delivery to work. Required: project_id, branch_id. Optional: enabled, otp_expires_in. Returns the updated NeonAuthPhoneNumberConfig.

params.name: enabled
params.description: Whether the phone number plugin is enabled.

params.name: otp_expires_in
params.description: Time in seconds before the OTP expires

tools.name: projects_branches_update-neon-auth-user-role
tools.description: Updates the role of a user in the Neon Auth user directory for the specified branch. The role controls the user's level of access within the Neon Auth integration. Required: project_id, branch_id, auth_user_id, roles. Returns the updated UpdateNeonAuthUserRoleResponse.

params.name: roles
params.description: Roles to assign to the user in the Neon Auth (Better Auth) directory. `user` and `admin` are the built-in roles; custom role strings are also supported.

tools.name: projects_branches_update-neon-auth-webhook-config
tools.description: Updates the webhook configuration for the specified branch's Neon Auth integration. Webhooks notify an external endpoint when auth events occur, such as user creation or sign-in. Required: project_id, branch_id, enabled. Optional: enabled_events, timeout_seconds (default: 5), webhook_url. Returns array of string.

params.name: enabled_events
params.description: Event types that trigger this webhook. Covers user lifecycle, email/OTP delivery, organization invitations, and phone verification events; see the enum for exact values.

params.name: timeout_seconds
params.description: Maximum time, in seconds, to wait for a response from the webhook endpoint.

params.name: webhook_url
params.description: Destination URL that receives webhook event payloads.

tools.name: projects_branches_update-project-branch
tools.description: Updates the specified branch. For more information, see [Manage branches](https://neon.com/docs/manage/branches/). Required: project_id, branch_id, branch. Returns the updated BranchOperations.

params.name: branch-expires-at
params.description: The timestamp when the branch is scheduled to expire and be automatically deleted. Must be set by the client following the [RFC 3339, section 5.6](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3339#section-5.6) format with precision up to seconds (such as 2025-06-09T18:02:16Z). Deletion is performed by a background job and may not occur exactly at the specified time. If this field is set to null, the expiration timestamp is removed. Access to this feature is currently limited to participants in the Early Access Program.

params.name: branch-name
params.description: New display name for the branch.

params.name: branch-protected
params.description: Whether the branch is protected. Protected branches (and their computes) cannot be deleted, archived, or reset, and block deletion of the project. Can be gated by `protected_branches_only` in the IP allowlist. Paid plans only.

tools.name: projects_branches_update-project-branch-data-api
tools.description: Updates the Neon Data API configuration for the specified branch. You can optionally provide settings to update the Data API configuration. The schema cache is always refreshed as part of this operation. Required: project_id, branch_id, database_name. Optional: settings. Returns the updated EmptyResponse.

params.name: settings-db-anon-role
params.description: Database role to use for anonymous requests

params.name: settings-db-extra-search-path
params.description: Extra schemas to add to the search path

params.name: settings-db-max-rows
params.description: Hard limit on the number of rows returned in a single Data API response. No limit when unset.

params.name: settings-db-schemas
params.description: List of schemas to expose via the API. Default: ['public']

params.name: settings-jwt-cache-max-lifetime
params.description: Maximum lifetime of the Data API's JWT cache, in seconds.

params.name: settings-jwt-role-claim-key
params.description: JWT claim key to use for role extraction

params.name: settings-server-timing-enabled
params.description: When enabled, the Data API adds `Server-Timing` headers to each response showing database execution and internal processing time. Default: disabled.

tools.name: projects_branches_update-project-branch-database
tools.description: Updates the specified database in the branch. For related information, see [Manage databases](https://neon.com/docs/manage/databases/). Required: project_id, branch_id, database_name, database. Returns the updated DatabaseOperations.

params.name: database-name
params.description: Name of the database to update.

params.name: database-owner-name
params.description: The name of the role that owns the database

tools.name: projects_branches_update-project-branch-function
tools.description: Updates the function's mutable metadata — currently only the display `name`. A string sets the display name; `null` clears it, after which the function's `name` falls back to its slug. Leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed; a whitespace-only name is rejected. Acts only on a function owned by the branch: a slug that is only inherited from an ancestor branch returns 404 — rename it on the branch that owns it. Like every other change on a branch, a rename is isolated per branch: a branch forked before the rename keeps the name it had at fork time. **Note**: This endpoint is currently in Beta. Required: project_id, branch_id, slug, name.

params.name: name
params.description: New display name for the function. `null` clears the display name; the function's `name` then falls back to its slug. Leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed; a whitespace-only name is rejected.

tools.name: projects_branches_update-project-branch-trigger
tools.description: Applies a partial update. The required `type` discriminator must identify the existing trigger kind. The supported types are `schedule` and `storage_object_created`. Editing an inherited trigger creates a child-local shadow with the same `trigger_id`; it remains disabled unless this request explicitly enables it. For a schedule trigger, updating the schedule or enabled state increments `version` and recomputes `next_run_at`. Disabling stops future scheduling but does not cancel occurrences already committed for delivery. For `storage_object_created`, the configuration selects one exact bucket. An omitted object-key prefix matches every key in that bucket; a present prefix is matched byte-for-byte and case-sensitively against the full key, without path normalization or a path-segment boundary. **Note**: This endpoint is currently in Beta. Required: project_id, branch_id, trigger_id. Returns the updated TriggerResponse.

tools.name: projects_connection-uri_get
tools.description: Retrieves a connection URI for the specified database. The URI uses the standard PostgreSQL connection string format. Set `pooled=true` to include the `-pooler` suffix for a connection pooler URI. Required: project_id, database_name, role_name. Optional: branch_id, endpoint_id, pooled. Returns the ConnectionUriresponse.

params.name: branch_id
params.description: The branch ID. Defaults to your project's default `branch_id` if not specified.

params.name: endpoint_id
params.description: The endpoint ID. Defaults to the read-write `endpoint_id` associated with the `branch_id` if not specified.

params.name: pooled
params.description: Adds the `-pooler` option to the connection URI when set to `true`, creating a pooled connection URI.

tools.name: projects_endpoints_create-project
tools.description: Creates a compute endpoint for the specified branch. A compute endpoint is a Neon compute instance. There is a maximum of one read-write compute endpoint per branch. If the specified branch already has a read-write compute endpoint, the operation fails. A branch can have multiple read-only compute endpoints. For more information about compute endpoints, see [Manage computes](https://neon.com/docs/manage/endpoints/). Required: project_id, endpoint. Returns the new EndpointOperations.

params.name: endpoint-branch-id
params.description: The ID of the branch the compute endpoint will be associated with

params.name: endpoint-disabled
params.description: Whether to restrict connections to the compute endpoint. Enabling this option schedules a suspend compute operation. A disabled compute endpoint cannot be enabled by a connection or console action. However, the compute endpoint is periodically enabled by check_availability operations.

params.name: endpoint-name
params.description: Optional name of the compute endpoint

params.name: endpoint-passwordless-access
params.description: NOT YET IMPLEMENTED. Whether to permit passwordless access to the compute endpoint.

params.name: endpoint-pooler-enabled
params.description: Deprecated. To enable connection pooling, append `-pooler` to the endpoint ID in the connection string. See [How to use connection pooling](https://neon.com/docs/connect/connection-pooling#how-to-use-connection-pooling)

params.name: endpoint-pooler-mode
params.description: Deprecated. The connection pooler mode. Neon supports PgBouncer in `transaction` mode only. Removal scheduled for June 20, 2026.

params.name: endpoint-region-id
params.description: The region where the compute endpoint will be created. Only the project's `region_id` is permitted.

params.name: endpoint-settings-pg-settings
params.description: A raw representation of Postgres settings

params.name: endpoint-settings-pgbouncer-settings
params.description: Deprecated. A raw representation of PgBouncer settings. Removal scheduled for June 20, 2026.

params.name: endpoint-settings-preload-libraries
params.description: The shared libraries to preload into the project's compute instances.

params.name: endpoint-suspend-timeout-seconds
params.description: Duration of inactivity in seconds after which the compute endpoint is automatically suspended. The value `0` means use the default value. The value `-1` means never suspend. For more information, see [Scale to zero configuration](https://neon.com/docs/manage/endpoints#scale-to-zero-configuration).

params.name: endpoint-type
params.description: Compute endpoint type. `read_write`: the primary read-write endpoint (one per branch). `read_only`: a read replica endpoint (multiple allowed per branch).

tools.name: projects_endpoints_delete-project
tools.description: Deletes the specified compute endpoint. A compute endpoint is a Neon compute instance. Deleting a compute endpoint drops existing network connections to the compute endpoint. The deletion is completed when the last operation in the chain finishes successfully. An `endpoint_id` has an `ep-` prefix. For information about compute endpoints, see [Manage computes](https://neon.com/docs/manage/endpoints/). Required: project_id, endpoint_id. Returns the EndpointOperations. Destructive.

tools.name: projects_endpoints_get-project
tools.description: Retrieves information about the specified compute endpoint. A compute endpoint is a Neon compute instance. An `endpoint_id` has an `ep-` prefix. For information about compute endpoints, see [Manage computes](https://neon.com/docs/manage/endpoints/). Required: project_id, endpoint_id. Returns the EndpointResponse.

tools.name: projects_endpoints_list-project
tools.description: Retrieves a list of compute endpoints for the specified project. A compute endpoint is a Neon compute instance. For information about compute endpoints, see [Manage computes](https://neon.com/docs/manage/endpoints/). Required: project_id. Returns array of Endpoint.

tools.name: projects_endpoints_restart-project
tools.description: Restarts the specified compute endpoint by immediately suspending it and then starting it again. An `endpoint_id` has an `ep-` prefix. For information about compute endpoints, see [Manage computes](https://neon.com/docs/manage/endpoints/). Required: project_id, endpoint_id. Returns the new EndpointOperations.

tools.name: projects_endpoints_start-project
tools.description: Starts a compute endpoint. The compute endpoint is ready to use after the last operation in the chain finishes successfully. An `endpoint_id` has an `ep-` prefix. For information about compute endpoints, see [Manage computes](https://neon.com/docs/manage/endpoints/). Required: project_id, endpoint_id. Returns the new EndpointOperations.

tools.name: projects_endpoints_suspend-project
tools.description: Suspends the specified compute endpoint. An `endpoint_id` has an `ep-` prefix. For information about compute endpoints, see [Manage computes](https://neon.com/docs/manage/endpoints/). Required: project_id, endpoint_id. Returns the new EndpointOperations.

If the compute endpoint was idle before the update, it becomes active for a short period of time, and the control plane suspends it again after the update. Required: project_id, endpoint_id, endpoint. Returns the updated EndpointOperations.

tools.name: projects_jwks_add-project
tools.description: Adds a JWKS URL to the specified project for verifying JWTs used as the authentication mechanism. The URL must be a valid HTTPS URL that returns a JSON Web Key Set. The `provider_name` field allows you to specify which authentication provider you're using (e.g., Clerk, Auth0, AWS Cognito). The `branch_id` scopes the JWKS URL to specific branches; if not specified, it applies to all branches. The `role_names` scopes the URL to specific roles; if not specified, default roles are used (`authenticator`, `authenticated`, `anonymous`). The `jwt_audience` specifies which `aud` values are accepted in JWTs. Required: project_id, jwks_url, provider_name. Optional: branch_id, jwt_audience, role_names (plus 1 more).

params.name: branch_id
params.description: The Neon branch ID. Returned as `id` from `GET /projects/{project_id}/branches`.

params.name: jwks_url
params.description: URL of the provider's JWKS endpoint used to verify JWTs.

params.name: jwt_audience
params.description: Expected `aud` claim in incoming JWTs. When set, tokens with a different audience are rejected; tokens with no audience are still accepted. Omit to skip audience validation.

params.name: provider_name
params.description: The name of the authentication provider (e.g., Clerk, Stytch, Auth0)

params.name: role_names
params.description: Deprecated. The roles the JWKS should be mapped to. By default, the JWKS is mapped to the `authenticator`, `authenticated`, and `anonymous` roles.

params.name: skip_role_creation
params.description: Deprecated. Only used with Neon RLS. If true, role creation is skipped.

tools.name: projects_jwks_delete-project
tools.description: Removes the specified JWKS URL from the project. JWTs signed by keys from the removed URL can no longer authenticate to the project's endpoints. Required: project_id, jwks_id. Returns array of string. Destructive.

tools.name: projects_jwks_get-project
tools.description: Returns the JWKS URLs available for verifying JWTs used as the authentication mechanism for the specified project. Required: project_id.

tools.name: projects_members_list-project
tools.description: Lists organization members and their per-project roles for an org-owned project. Returns 404 when the project is not org-owned, per-project role management is disabled, or the caller has no access. Callers with VIEWER or EDITOR see members with effective project access. Callers with ADMIN also see unassigned org members. Required: project_id. Optional: cursor, limit.

params.name: cursor
params.description: A cursor to use in pagination.

params.name: limit
params.description: The maximum number of members to return in the response

tools.name: projects_members_remove-project-role
tools.description: Idempotently removes the explicit project grant. The member's organization-role default project permission still applies. Self-DELETE requires `confirm_self_lockout=true` when effective manage access would be lost. Required: project_id, member_id. Optional: confirm_self_lockout. Returns the ProjectMemberRoleResponse. Destructive.

tools.name: projects_members_set-project-role
tools.description: Idempotently sets or updates the explicit project grant of the specified org member. Self-demotion requires `confirm_self_demotion=true`. Required: project_id, member_id, role. Optional: confirm_self_demotion. Returns the updated ProjectMemberRoleResponse.

params.name: role
params.description: Per-project role. `viewer` maps to `VIEWER`, `editor` maps to `EDITOR`, and `admin` maps to `ADMIN`.

tools.name: projects_operations_get-project
tools.description: Retrieves details for the specified operation. An operation is an action performed on a Neon project resource. Required: project_id, operation_id. Returns the OperationResponse.

tools.name: projects_operations_list-project
tools.description: Retrieves a list of operations for the specified Neon project. The number of operations returned can be large. To paginate the response, issue an initial request with a `limit` value. Then, add the `cursor` value that was returned in the response to the next request. Operations older than 6 months may be deleted from our systems. If you need more history than that, you should store your own history. Required: project_id. Optional: cursor, limit. Returns the OperationsListProjectResponse.

params.name: cursor
params.description: Specify the cursor value from the previous response to get the next batch of operations

params.name: limit
params.description: Specify a value from 1 to 1000 to limit number of operations in the response

tools.name: projects_permissions_grant-to-project
tools.description: Grants project access to the account associated with the specified email address. Required: project_id, email. Returns the new ProjectPermission.

params.name: email
params.description: Email address of the user to grant project access to.

tools.name: projects_permissions_list-project
tools.description: Retrieves details about users who have access to the project, including the permission `id`, the granted-to email address, and the date project access was granted. Required: project_id. Returns array of ProjectPermission.

tools.name: projects_permissions_revoke-from-project
tools.description: Revokes project access from the user associated with the specified permission `id`. You can retrieve a user's permission `id` by listing project access. Required: project_id, permission_id. Returns the ProjectPermission. Destructive.

tools.name: projects_recover_project
tools.description: Recovers a deleted project within the 7-day deletion recovery period. Restores branches, endpoints, settings, and connection strings. Some integrations require manual reconfiguration after recovery. To list recoverable projects, use `GET /projects?recoverable=true`. Required: project_id. Returns the new ProjectRecoverResponse.

tools.name: projects_snapshots_delete
tools.description: Deletes the specified snapshot. Required: project_id, snapshot_id. Returns array of Operation. Destructive.

tools.name: projects_snapshots_list
tools.description: Lists the snapshots for the specified project. Each snapshot represents a point-in-time backup of the project data. Required: project_id. Returns array of Snapshot.

tools.name: projects_snapshots_restore
tools.description: Restores the specified snapshot to a new branch, and optionally finalizes the restore operation to replace the original branch. Required: project_id, snapshot_id. Optional: name, finalize_restore (default: false), name (plus 1 more). Returns the new SnapshotsRestoreResponse.

params.name: name
params.description: Deprecated. Use the `name` field in the request body instead. Removal scheduled for November 29, 2025. A name for the newly restored branch. If omitted, a default name will be generated.

params.name: finalize_restore
params.description: Set to `true` to finalize the restore operation immediately. This will complete the restore and move any associated computes to the new branch, similar to the `finalizeRestoreBranch` operation. Defaults to `false` to allow previewing the restored snapshot data first.

params.name: name-2
params.description: A name for the newly restored branch. If not provided, the server generates a unique name for the branch automatically.

params.name: target_branch_id
params.description: ID of the branch to restore the snapshot into. Defaults to the snapshot's source branch (`snapshot.source_branch_id`); fails if that cannot be determined.

tools.name: projects_snapshots_update
tools.description: Updates the specified snapshot. Required: project_id, snapshot_id, snapshot. Returns the updated SnapshotsUpdateResponse.

params.name: snapshot-expires-at
params.description: The date and time when the snapshot will expire. Omit to leave the current expiration unchanged. Send `null` to clear the expiration so the snapshot never expires. A future timestamp sets the absolute expiration.

tools.name: projects_transfer-requests_accept-project
tools.description: Accepts a transfer request for the specified project, transferring it to the specified organization or user. If org_id is not passed, the project will be transferred to the current user or organization account. Required: project_id, request_id. Optional: org_id.

params.name: request_id
params.description: The Neon project transfer request ID

params.name: org_id
params.description: The Neon organization ID to transfer the project to. If not provided, the project will be transferred to the current user or organization account.

tools.name: projects_transfer-requests_create-project
tools.description: Creates a transfer request for the specified project. The request expires after a set period. To accept the request, the recipient calls `PUT /projects/{project_id}/transfer_requests/{request_id}` or uses the Neon Console claim link. The optional `ru` parameter redirects the recipient after acceptance. Required: project_id. Optional: ttl_seconds (default: 86400). Returns the new ProjectTransferRequestResponse.

params.name: ttl_seconds
params.description: Number of seconds the transfer request stays valid before it expires. Defaults to 86400 (24 hours).

tools.name: projects_vpc-endpoints_assign-project
tools.description: Sets or updates a VPC endpoint restriction for a Neon project. When a VPC endpoint restriction is set, the project only accepts connections from the specified VPC. A VPC endpoint can be set as a restriction only after it is assigned to the parent organization of the Neon project. Required: project_id, vpc_endpoint_id, label.

params.name: label
params.description: Human-readable name for the VPC endpoint assignment, used to identify it within the organization.

tools.name: projects_vpc-endpoints_delete-project
tools.description: Removes the specified VPC endpoint restriction from a Neon project. Required: project_id, vpc_endpoint_id. Destructive.

tools.name: projects_vpc-endpoints_list-project
tools.description: Lists VPC endpoint restrictions for the specified Neon project. Required: project_id. Returns array of Vpcendpoint.

tools.name: regions_get-active
tools.description: Lists supported Neon regions. **Note:** Not all regions are available to all organizations. Pass the `org_id` parameter to get an accurate list of regions available to your organization. Optional: org_id. Returns array of RegionResponse.

params.name: org_id
params.description: Organization ID. When provided, returns only regions available to this organization. Recommended for accurate region availability.

tools.name: users_get-current-info
tools.description: Retrieves information about the currently authenticated Neon user, including account identifiers, plan details, and linked auth accounts. Returns array of CurrentUserAuthAccount.

tools.name: users_get-current-organizations
tools.description: Retrieves the organizations that the currently authenticated user belongs to. When called with an organization- or project-scoped API key (which is not tied to a user), this returns the single organization that owns the key.

tools.name: users_transfer-projects-from-to-org
tools.description: Deprecated. Personal accounts have been migrated to organizations, so this operation no longer applies. Removal scheduled for July 1, 2026. Required: destination_org_id, project_ids. Returns the new EmptyResponse.

params.name: project_ids
params.description: The list of projects ids to transfer. Maximum of 400 project ids

novel_features.name: Stale branches
novel_features.description: Find idle or expired branches across every project from the local mirror (run sync first), with delete commands for non-default branches.

novel_features.name: Fleet tree
novel_features.description: See every org, project, branch and compute in one hierarchy from the local mirror (run sync first).

novel_features.name: Usage trends
novel_features.description: Track compute, storage and transfer per project with period-over-period deltas; on plans without consumption history (below Launch/Scale) it uses per-sync snapshots (basis: sync-snapshots).

novel_features.name: Usage top
novel_features.description: Rank projects by compute, storage, transfer or written data; on plans without consumption history it ranks period-to-date totals from sync snapshots (basis: sync-snapshots).

novel_features.name: Operation wait
novel_features.description: Block until a branch's async operations finish; exits 0 when done, 6 if an operation failed, 8 on timeout.

novel_features.name: Preview branch up
novel_features.description: Create a real branch (or reuse an existing one by name), wait until ready and print its connection string; --expires applies only to newly created branches.

novel_features.name: Branch prune
novel_features.description: Preview idle or expired branches to delete (from the local mirror); --yes actually deletes them, always skipping default and protected branches.

novel_features.name: Compute audit
novel_features.description: Flag computes that never scale to zero, have fixed autoscaling, or are oversized on non-default branches, from the local mirror (run sync first).
